evidence.claim: Cameco says its fuel-services division includes the Blind River refinery, about 18% of world UF6 primary conversion capacity at Port Hope, and CANDU fuel assembly/reactor-component manufacturing at Port Hope and Cobourg.
Cameco describes the Port Hope conversion facility as one of three Western suppliers of UF6, the feedstock for enrichment plants producing light-water-reactor fuel.
The NRC states Centrus has one active enrichment facility license and that ACO signed a DOE contract to deploy 16 centrifuges to demonstrate HALEU production up to 19.75% U-235.
evidence.source_title: Centrus Energy Corp./American Centrifuge Operating, LLC Gas Centrifuge Enrichment Facility Licensing | NRC

memory_update.text: LEU should remain the primary U.S.-listed public candidate for domestic HALEU/enrichment exposure, but survival to later layers requires DOE task-order and commercial offtake verification.
XE is newly U.S.-listed and should be tracked as a fuel-fabrication chokepoint candidate, not only as an SMR/reactor developer, because TRISO-X has an NRC Part 70 HALEU fuel-fabrication license.
ASPI is a speculative shadow candidate only; keep it in Layer 1B because of possible HALEU enrichment optionality, but require NRC/DOE/customer evidence before upgrading.

For this node, separate mining, conversion, enrichment, deconversion, and fuel fabrication. Cameco is useful as a conversion/fuel-services reference even though it is too large and high-attention for the underfollowed lane.

Potential omitted public names for a follow-up pass: BWXT for TRISO/deconversion/fuel fabrication and Silex/GLE via non-standard or OTC/Australia exposure; verify U.S.-listed accessibility and purity before adding.
